\chapter{Strategy observables and the expanded space}
\label{chap:qpbt-observables}
% This chapter covers the first three subsections of the source appendix
% ``Analysis of the Pauli basis test''
% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, lines 1-679).
% The paper's subsection labels sec:qld-prelim, sec:commutation and
% sec:expanding are kept on the sections below for cross-reference fidelity.
% The source restates thm:pauli verbatim at the head of the appendix under the
% label thm:pauli-appendix (lines 6-20); the statement is the same theorem, and
% all references here are to thm:pauli as stated in Chapter chap:qpbt-test.

This chapter and the two that follow contain the proof of the soundness
theorem for the Pauli basis test, Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}, stated in
Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-test}. Starting from a strategy that succeeds in the
game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{Pauli}}_{(q,m,d)}$ with high probability, the proof
constructs a representation of the Pauli group on the players' Hilbert space
in several stages. In Section~\ref{sec:commutation} the strategy measurements
are used to define a set of observables that correspond to a subset of the
Pauli $X$ and $Z$ observables, and these observables are shown to
approximately satisfy the associated Pauli group relations. In
Section~\ref{sec:expanding}, ancillary registers containing EPR states are
adjoined to the players' state, and a new set of approximately commuting
observables acting on the expanded state is defined.
Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-combining} combines the approximately commuting
observables into a strategy for the \emph{classical} low individual degree
test and applies the soundness theorem of that test to construct a single
projective measurement that simultaneously measures all of them.
Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} uses this simultaneous measurement to
construct an exact representation of the Pauli group, shows that it is close
to the original strategy observables on the expanded state, and deduces
Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}. Section~\ref{sec:qld-prelim} below collects
preliminary definitions and lemmas used throughout the analysis.

\section{Preliminaries}
\label{sec:qld-prelim}

\begin{definition}[Individual and total degree polynomial classes]
	\label{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
	\uses{def:line, def:line-representative, def:polyfunc}
	Given integers $d, m \geq 0$ and a prime power $q$, denote by
	$\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables over
	$\F_q$ with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When
	the field is clear from context we write $\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}$, and when
	the number of variables is also clear from context, $\mathrm{ideg}_d$. We
	denote by $\deg_d$ the set of polynomials with \emph{total} degree at
	most $d$.
	% The line-restricted classes below are introduced only implicitly in the
	% source, in the statement of the lemma labelled lem:qld-comm-line-cons,
	% which reads them as polynomials "defined on the line". The coefficient
	% reading adopted here follows the answer format of the decision procedure
	% of the low individual degree game (source figure fig:ld-decider) and the
	% representative convention of def:polyfunc; see the remark following this
	% definition.
	For a line $\ell \subseteq \F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line}) presented
	by a base point $u_0$ and a direction $v$ --- for the lines arising as
	question contents, the pair read off the line's description, whose base
	point is the canonical representative of
	Definition~\ref{def:line-representative} --- and an integer $c \geq 0$,
	we write $\deg_c(\ell)$ for the set of univariate polynomials of degree
	at most $c$, each given by its list of $c+1$ coefficients and identified
	by its polynomial representative rather than by the function it induces,
	as in Definition~\ref{def:polyfunc}; the argument $\ell$ records the
	line to which such an answer refers, through the parameterization
	$t \mapsto u_0 + tv$. The cases used below are $\deg_d(\ell)$ and
	$\deg_{md}(\ell)$; whenever $d \leq md$, extending coefficient lists by
	zeros gives the inclusion $\deg_d(\ell) \subseteq \deg_{md}(\ell)$. For
	$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$, $u \in \ell$, and $a \in \F_q$, we say that $f$
	\emph{evaluates to $a$ at $u$}, written $f(u) = a$, if $f(t) = a$ for
	every $t \in \F_q$ with $u = u_0 + tv$. When $v \neq 0$ this $t$ is
	unique, so every $f$ evaluates at every point of $\ell$; when $v = 0$,
	so that $\ell = \{u_0\}$, exactly those $f$ that induce a constant
	function on $\F_q$ evaluate at $u_0$, to their constant value. An
	operator indexed by $f(u)$ is understood to be the zero operator when
	$f$ does not evaluate at $u$, and for a family $\{N_f\}$ indexed by
	$f \in \deg_c(\ell)$ we write
	$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=a]} = \sum_{f \colon f(u) = a} N_f$; when
	$v = 0$ the classes indexed by $a \in \F_q$ form a sub-measurement
	rather than a partition of the outcomes. The \emph{completed} family of
	evaluation classes is the family indexed by $a \in \F_q \cup \{\bot\}$
	obtained by adjoining the additional class
	$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]} = \sum_{f} N_f$, the sum over those
	$f$ that do not evaluate at $u$; when $\{N_f\}$ is a POVM,
	respectively a projective measurement, the completed classes form one
	as well, and when $v \neq 0$ the class
	$N_{[\mathrm{eval}_u(\cdot)=\bot]}$ is the zero operator.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[Line answers as coefficient lists]
	\label{rem:deg-line-representatives}
	The source refers to the elements of $\deg_{md}(\ell)$ as polynomials
	``defined on the line $\ell$'', that is, as functions on the point set
	of $\ell$, while its decision procedure expects each line answer as a
	list of coefficients. The two readings differ. When $md \geq q$,
	distinct coefficient lists induce the same function $\F_q \to \F_q$;
	and when $\ell$ has direction $v = 0$ --- a case the question
	distributions produce with positive probability
	(Remark~\ref{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}) --- the point set of $\ell$ is
	the singleton $\{u_0\}$, so a function on $\ell$ retains only a single
	field element of the answer. Definition~\ref{def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
	therefore adopts the coefficient reading, under which the strategy's
	line measurements are indexed by exactly the answers of the prescribed
	form, and its evaluation convention reproduces the universal
	quantification of the line-versus-point clauses of the win predicates
	(Definition~\ref{def:ld-win-predicate}).
\end{remark}

Throughout this chapter $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size
(Definition~\ref{def:admissible-size}) and $M = 2^m$ is the number of
$q$-ary qudits tested for per player, as in
Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-test} and~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction}. (The letter
$M$ also denotes the measurement operators of the strategy under analysis,
as in the tuple $\mathcal{S} = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ below and in the
super- and subscripted individual operators such as
$M^{(\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a$; the meaning is determined by context, as in
the source.) Recall from
Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} the low-degree code
(see Definition~\ref{def:low-degree-encoding}), which maps each vector
$h \in \F_q^{M}$, with
coordinates indexed by binary strings of length $m$, to a polynomial
$g_h \in \mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\F_q)$ such that $g_h(u) = h_u$ for every
$u \in \{0,1\}^m$; for $x \in \F_q^m$ the associated vector

$g_h(x) = h \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(x)$ for all $h$. Recall also the finite

(see Definition~\ref{def:subfield-trace}).

\begin{definition}[Commuting and anticommuting tuples]
	\label{def:anticommuting-tuple}
	% The quantity gamma is introduced in the source at eq:gamma-value, inside
	% the completeness analysis of the Pauli basis test; the definition below
	% is self-contained and does not depend on that occurrence.
	\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:subfield-trace}
	For a tuple
	$\omega = (u_X, u_Z, r_X, r_Z) \in (\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$, let
	\[
		\gamma(\omega) \,=\, \tr\big( (r_X \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_X)) \cdot (r_Z \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)) \big)\,,
	\]
	where $r_W \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_W)$ is the scalar multiple of the
	vector $\mathrm{ind}_m(u_W) \in \F_q^{M}$, the middle $\cdot$ is the
	$\F_q$-inner product of two vectors in $\F_q^{M}$, and
	$\tr = \tr_{q \to 2}$. The tuple $\omega$ is called \emph{anticommuting}
	if $\gamma(\omega) \neq 0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma(\omega) = 0$.
\end{definition}

The sign $(-1)^{\gamma(\omega)}$ is exactly the sign with which the
generalized Pauli observables $\tau^X(r_X \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_X))$ and
$\tau^Z(r_Z \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z))$ commute
(see Lemma~\ref{lem:twisted-commutation});
this is the source of the terminology.

\begin{lemma}[Probability of anticommuting tuples]
	\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
	% The source states this result in a `fact' environment; it is stated here
	% as a lemma, and the paper label is kept verbatim.
	% The exact value of the anticommuting probability and the constant lower
	% bounds under the hypothesis m <= q are additions relative to the source,
	% which asserts only the two bounds displayed at the end of the statement;
	% the source states those bounds without the hypothesis m, d >= 1, under
	% which alone they hold (see the remark following this lemma). The
	% unconditional constant bounds are what the proof of the lemma labelled
	% lem:qld-win-implications uses.
	\uses{def:anticommuting-tuple}
	A tuple $\omega = (u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)$ sampled uniformly at random from
	$(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$ is anticommuting with probability exactly
	\[
		\big(1 - q^{-1}\big)^{m+1} \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
	\]
	and commuting with the complementary probability, which is at least
	$\frac12$. In particular, if $m \leq q$, then $\omega$ is anticommuting
	with probability at least $2^{-4}$ and commuting with probability at
	least $\frac12$. If $m, d \geq 1$, then the probability that $\omega$ is
	anticommuting is at least
	\[
		(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big(1 - \frac{md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}
		\,\geq\, \Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\Big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}\,,
	\]
	and the probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least
	$\big(1 - \frac{3md}{q}\big) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\uses{def:low-degree-encoding, def:indicator-vector, def:admissible-size, def:binary-representation, lem:downsize_field, lem:one}
	By the definition of the indicator vector
	(Definition~\ref{def:indicator-vector}), expanding the product over the
	coordinates $i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ into a sum over $y \in \{0,1\}^m$
	gives
	\[
		\mathrm{ind}_m(u_X) \cdot \mathrm{ind}_m(u_Z)
		\,=\, \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_X)\, \mathrm{ind}_{m,y}(u_Z)
		\,=\, \prod_{i=1}^{m} \big( u_{X,i}\, u_{Z,i} + (1 - u_{X,i})(1 - u_{Z,i}) \big)\,,
	\]
	and since $\F_q$ has characteristic $2$, the $i$-th factor equals
	$1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$. Hence
	\[
		\gamma(\omega) \,=\, \tr\Big( (r_X r_Z) \cdot \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}) \Big)\,.
	\]
	For any fixed $u_X$, the $m$ factors $1 + u_{X,i} + u_{Z,i}$ are

	(Definition~\ref{def:binary-representation}), item~2 of
	Lemma~\ref{lem:downsize_field} gives
	$\tr(c) = \tr(c \cdot 1) = \kappa(c) \cdot \kappa(1)$, and $\kappa(1)$

	a product of two positive functions of $q$ that are nondecreasing for

	hence the anticommuting probability is at least $2^{-4}$.

# API surface for `SubMeas` obligations

Focused on the declarations that help prove the usual `SubMeas` goals:

- PSD / Hermitian facts
- pointwise bounds such as `A.outcome a ≤ A.total` or `≤ 1`
- sum identities and transport of those obligations through postprocessing / tensor placement / completion

## `MIPStarRE/Quantum.lean`

`Quantum.lean` itself defines no declarations. It is a re-export file:

```lean
import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Basic
import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Order
import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.TracePairing
import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.BlockDiagonal
import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace
import MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement
```

Relevant re-exported API:

### From `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`

`MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix` is now an aggregate import.  For direct
dependencies, use the mathematical leaves:

- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Basic`
  - `Op`, trace reindexing, `Matrix.submatrixLinearMap`, and elementary
    Kronecker bookkeeping.
- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Order`
  - positive-semidefinite order, the closed PSD cone, trace norm control,
    sandwich monotonicity, `sq_le_self`, Kronecker monotonicity, and reindexing
    positivity.
- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.TracePairing`
  - continuous real trace pairings, Hermitian representatives of continuous
    real-linear functionals, weak-duality positivity, and complementary
    slackness algebra.
- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.BlockDiagonal`
  - the linear-map form of `Matrix.blockDiagonal`, block-diagonal positivity,
    and the corresponding block trace identity.
- `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace`
  - normalized trace, `tauNormSq`, projections, and spectral truncation.

- `abbrev MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (d : Type*) := Matrix d d ℂ`
  - The operator type used everywhere in `SubMeas`.

- `def Matrix.submatrixLinearMap (R : Type*) (row : m' → m) (col : n' → n) :
  Matrix m n α →ₗ[R] Matrix m' n' α`
  - The linear-map form of `Matrix.submatrix`; use this for diagonal-block
    projections and other coordinate restrictions instead of reproving
    additivity entry by entry.

- `theorem sandwich_nonneg {M P : Op d} (hP : 0 ≤ P) (hMH : Mᴴ = M) : 0 ≤ M * P * M`
  - PSD is preserved under Hermitian sandwiching.

- `theorem sandwich_mono {M P Q : Op d} (hMH : Mᴴ = M) (hPQ : P ≤ Q) : M * P * M ≤ M * Q * M`
  - Monotonicity under sandwiching.

- `theorem sq_le_self [DecidableEq d] {X : Op d} (hX : 0 ≤ X) (hXle : X ≤ 1) : X * X ≤ X`
  - Standard `0 ≤ X ≤ 1` consequence.

- `noncomputable def normalizedTrace (A : Op d) : ℂ`
- `theorem normalizedTrace_add (A B : Op d) : normalizedTrace (A + B) = normalizedTrace A + normalizedTrace B`
- `theorem normalizedTrace_sub (A B : Op d) : normalizedTrace (A - B) = normalizedTrace A - normalizedTrace B`
- `theorem normalizedTrace_smul (c : ℂ) (A : Op d) : normalizedTrace (c • A) = c * normalizedTrace A`
- `theorem normalizedTrace_mul_comm (A B : Op d) : normalizedTrace (A * B) = normalizedTrace (B * A)`
  - Trace linearity/cyclicity tools used downstream for scalarized sum arguments.

- `noncomputable def tauNormSq (A : Op d) : ℂ`
- `structure IsProj (P : Op d) : Prop`
- `structure SpectralTruncation (source target : Op d) : Prop`
  - Less direct for basic `SubMeas` obligations, but part of the operator API.

    48	\label{sec:qld-prelim}
    49	
    50	
    51	\begin{definition}
    52	Given integer $d,m$ and a prime power $q$ we denote by $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ the set of polynomials in $m$ variables
    53	  with \emph{individual} degree at most $d$ in each variable. When the field is clear from context we write $\ideg_{d,m}$. 	
    54		When
    55	  the number of variables is clear from context we
    56	  write $\ideg_d$. We denote by $\deg_{d}$ the set of polynomials with
    57	  \emph{total} degree at most $d$.
    58	\end{definition}
    59	
    60	Recall the low-degree code defined in \Cref{sec:ld-encoding}, in which vectors $h \in \F_q^\nqubits$ get mapped to polynomials $g_h \in \ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$ such that for every $u \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_h(u) = h_u$ where the coordinates of $h$ are indexed by binary strings of length $m$. For $x\in \F_q^m$, recall the definition of the vector $\ind_m(x) \in \F_q^\nqubits$ from Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}. Recall also the finite field trace $\tr(\cdot)=\tr_{q\to 2}(\cdot):\F_q\to\F_2$, where $q=2^k$ for odd $k$, defined in Section~\ref{sec:subfields}. 
    61	
    62	
    63	
    64	Call a tuple $\omega = (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) \in (\F_q^m)^2
    65	\times (\F_q)^2$ \emph{anticommuting} if the quantity 
    66	 \[\gamma\,=\,\tr ((r_\xpt \cdot
    67	\ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt)))\]
    68	introduced in~\Cref{eq:gamma-value} is not $0$, and \emph{commuting} if $\gamma=0$.
    69	
    70	\begin{fact}
    71	\label{fact:omega-anticomm-prob}
    72		The probability that a tuple $\omega= (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$ sampled uniformly at random from $(\F_q^m)^2 \times (\F_q)^2$
    73		is anti-commuting is at least 
    74		\[
    75			(1 - q^{-m}) \cdot (1 - q^{-1}) \cdot \Big (1 - \frac{md}{q} \Big )  \cdot \frac{1}{2} \geq \Big (1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}.
    76		\]
    77		The probability that $\omega$ is commuting is also at least $\Big(1 - \frac{3md}{q} \Big ) \cdot \frac{1}{2}$.
    78	\end{fact}
    79	\begin{proof}
    80		First, note that $\ind_m(u_\xpt) = 0$ if and only if $u_\xpt = 0$. If $u_\xpt=0$ then $\omega$ is commuting. Otherwise, if $u_\xpt \neq 0$, then observe that for all $r_\xpt, r_\zpt, u_\zpt$,
    81		\begin{align*}
    82			\tr( (r_\xpt \cdot \ind_m(u_\xpt)) \cdot (r_\zpt \cdot
    83	                \ind_m(u_\zpt))) &= \tr( r_\xpt r_\zpt (\ind_m(u_\xpt) \cdot \ind_m(u_\zpt))) \\
    84									&= \tr( (r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt))\;,
    85		\end{align*}
    86		where $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}$ is a nonzero polynomial in $\ideg_{d,m}(\F_q)$.
    87		
    88		If $r_\xpt = 0$, then $\omega$ is commuting. Condition on $r_\xpt \neq 0$.  Since $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}\neq 0$ has total degree at most $md$, by the Schwartz-Zippel lemma the probability that $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is zero over a uniformly random choice of $u_\zpt$ is at most $md/q$. Conditioned on $g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt) \neq 0$, the product $(r_\xpt r_\zpt) \cdot g_{\ind_m(u_\xpt)}(u_\zpt)$ is a uniformly random element of $\F_q$ when $r_\zpt$ is chosen uniformly at random.

    95	In this appendix we often use the ``$\approx_\delta$'' notation to specify closeness of general operators (not necessarily POVMs) that are indexed by questions but not answers: given sets of operators $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ indexed by questions $x \in \cal{X}$, we write $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ to denote \[
    96		\E_{x \sim \mu} \bra{\psi} (A^x - B^x)^\dagger (A^x - B^x)
    97	        \ket{\psi}\,\leq\, O(\delta)
    98	      \]
    99	where $\mu$ is a question distribution and $\ket{\psi}$ is a state that has been fixed by context. This will be useful for expressing closeness of observables, for example. The following two lemmas relate the closeness between sets of operators and weighted sums of those operators. 
   100	\begin{lemma}
   101	\label{lem:avg-closeness}
   102	Let $\{A^x \}$ and $\{B^x\}$ be operators indexed by some finite set $\mathcal{X}$, and let $\mu$ be a probability distribution over $\mathcal{X}$. Let $\{\alpha_x \}$ be a set of complex numbers such that $|\alpha_x| \leq 1$. Then if $A^x \approx_\delta B^x$ on average over $x$ drawn from $\mu$, then $A \approx_\delta B$, where $A = \E_x \alpha_x A^x$ and $B= \E_x \alpha_x B^x$.
   103	\end{lemma}
   104	\begin{proof}
   105	Expand
   106	\begin{align*}
   107		\Big\| \E_x \alpha_x \big ( A^x - B^x \big) \ket{\psi} \Big\|^2 &\leq \Big( \E_x \norm{ (A^x -B^x) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   108		&\leq \E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   109		&\leq \delta\;.
   110	\end{align*}
   111	The first inequality is the triangle inequality and the second inequality is Jensen's inequality. 
   112	\end{proof}

   114	\begin{lemma}
   115	\label{lem:povm-to-obs}
   116	Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set. Let $\{A^x_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ and $\{B^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be POVMs and let $\{ \alpha_a \}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}$ be a collection of complex numbers on the unit circle. Let $A^x = \sum_a \alpha_a A^x_a$ and $B^x = \sum_a  \alpha_a B^x_a$. Then 
   117	\[
   118		A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a \quad \text{implies} \quad A^x \approx_{\delta'} B^x
   119	\]
   120	for $\delta' = |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta$.
   121	\end{lemma}
   122	\begin{proof}
   123	Expand
   124		\begin{align*}
   125			\E_x \norm{(A^x - B^x) \ket{\psi}}^2 &= \E_x \Big\|\sum_a \alpha_a (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}\Big\|^2 \\
   126			&\leq \E_x \Big( \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}} \Big)^2 \\
   127			&\leq \E_x |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \sum_a \norm{ (A^x_a - B^x_a) \ket{\psi}}^2 \\
   128			&\leq |\mathcal{A}| \cdot \delta\;.
   129		\end{align*}
   130	The first inequality follows from the triangle inequality, the second inequality follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, and the last inequality follows from the assumption that $A^x_a \approx_\delta B^x_a$. 
   131	\end{proof}

   616	                   \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) = a]}  \ot (I - \hat{M}^{(\Point, W), u}_{a})
   617	                   \ket{\hat{\psi}},

   639	For projective sub-measurements $\{A_i\}$ and $\{B_i\}$ and a state $\ket{\varphi}$,

   663	      the third line, to remove the square. Thus

   665	        \delta\;, \]

   667	      Item~1 of \Cref{fact:agreement}, this in turn implies that $A^x_i \ot I
   668	      \approx_\delta I \ot B^x_i$. Applying this fact to the projective
   669	      measurements $\{ (\hat{M}^{(\Line, W), \line}_{[\eval_u(\cdot) =
   670	        a]})_{\alice \alice'} \}_a$ and $\{(\hat{M}^{(\Point,W),
   671	        u}_{a})_{\bob \alice''}\}$ in~\eqref{eq:qld-comm-line-2} gives

   675	      Taking the function $\delta_{\Line}$ in the lemma to be $\sqrt{\eps}$,
   676	      this yields the conclusion of \Cref{eq:qld-comm-line-pt-cons2}
   677	      of the lemma.
   678	\end{proof}

   429	$(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\alice \alice'}$ or $(\hat{W}^r(u))_{\bob
   430	  \alice''}$).
   431	
   432	
   433	
   434	\paragraph{Partitioning the registers, and symmetries}
   435	In the remainder of this section as well as \Cref{sec:combining,sec:apply-ldt}, we will partition the six registers
   436	$\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''$ into
   437	two ``parties'' in two different ways. The first is to consider
   438	$\alice \alice'$ together to form  a single party, and $\bob \alice''$
   439	to form the second party. The second is to consider $\bob \bob'$ to
   440	form the first party, and $\alice \bob''$ to form the second
   441	party. Thanks to the symmetry of the Pauli basis test under exchanging the
   442	two players, as well as the symmetry of the ancilla states in
   443	registers $\alice' \alice''$ and $\bob' \bob''$, every ``bipartite'' consistency relation we derive between two
   444	operators $M, N$ will hold for both of the two bipartitioning schemes,
   445	and with the first and second party interchanged. That is, whenever we
   446	derive a bipartite relation of the form
   447	\[ M_{\alice \alice'} \approx_\delta N_{\bob \alice''}, \]
   448	the same steps, with the registers appropriately changed, will also
   449	yield
   450	\begin{align*}
   451	  N_{\alice \alice'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\bob \alice''}, \\
   452	  M_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} N_{\alice \bob''}, \\
   453	  N_{\bob \bob'} &\approx_{\delta} M_{\alice \bob''}.
   454	\end{align*}
   455	
   456	Similarly, whenever we derive a single-party relation of the form
   457	$M_{\alice \alice'} \approx N_{\alice \alice'}$, the same steps with
   458	the registers appropriately changed will also yield the same relation
   459	on $\bob\alice''$, $\bob \bob'$ and $\alice \bob''$. We refer to these
   460	relations as \emph{symmetric equivalents}.

     3	/-!
     4	# Pauli basis test soundness
     5	
     6	The quantitative error function and the source-shaped soundness statement live
     7	here.  All analytic estimates are intentionally proof-level obligations in the
     8	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
     9	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    16	The distance functionals use `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` from
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    25	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    30	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,
    31	as specified by `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`,
    32	paper `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
    33	-/
    34	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    35	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    36	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    37	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
    38	
    39	/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a
    40	Lean-only helper for the operator conclusion of `thm:pauli`; it uses the
    41	matrix representation of the isometry and its conjugate transpose.  Blueprint
    42	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    44	-/
    45	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    46	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    47	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    48	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    49	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    50	  U * M * Uᴴ
    51	
    52	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the
    53	coordinate form of the tensor-register shuffle used in the paper's ideal
    54	state (`def:EPR`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`),
    55	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
    56	-/
    57	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    58	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    59	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    60	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    61	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    62	
    63	/-- Coordinate tensoring of two local maps on a bipartite state.  The formula
    64	is a genuine finite sum over the input coordinates; preservation of the norm
    65	is part of the later soundness proof for `thm:pauli`, blueprint
    66	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
    67	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
    68	-/
    69	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    70	    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' R : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    72	    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    73	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    74	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × R))
    75	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × R))
    76	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    77	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) :=
    78	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) ℂ).symm
    79	    (fun p =>
    80	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    81	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × R) ℂ)
    82	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    83	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιB' × R) ℂ)
    84	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    85	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)) )
    86	
    87	/-- The ideal auxiliary state `aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}` in the shuffled register
    88	ordering.  The EPR factor is the concrete `eprState` from
    89	`def:EPR` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper
    90	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`).
    91	-/
    92	noncomputable def idealState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    93	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    94	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    95	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    96	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
    97	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) ×
    98	      (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    99	    (fun p =>
   100	      ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ) aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
   101	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P) ℂ)
   102	          (eprState (PauliRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
   103	
   104	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
   105	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   107	-/
   108	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   109	  (.pauli W, 0)
   110	
   111	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and
   112	B-side registers.  This is a concrete matrix form of the operator comparison
   113	in `thm:pauli` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper
   114	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`).
   115	-/
   116	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   117	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   118	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   119	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   120	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   121	  fun p q =>
   122	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
   123	      pauliProj W u p.1.2 q.1.2
   124	    else 0
   125	
   126	/-- The symmetric B-side ideal Pauli projector from `thm:pauli`, blueprint
   127	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   128	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   129	-/
   130	noncomputable def pauliProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   131	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   132	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
   133	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
   134	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   135	  fun p q =>
   136	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
   137	      pauliProj W u p.2.2 q.2.2
   138	    else 0
   139	
   140	/-- Lift a conjugated A-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   141	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   142	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def liftedAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   145	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   146	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   147	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   148	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   149	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
   150	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   151	  fun p q =>
   152	    if p.2 = q.2 then
   153	      (conjIsometry φA M) p.1 q.1
   154	    else 0
   155	
   156	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   157	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   158	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   159	-/
   160	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   161	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   162	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   163	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   164	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   165	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   166	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   167	  fun p q =>
   168	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   169	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   170	    else 0
   171	
   172	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   173	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   174	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   175	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   176	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   177	-/
   178	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   179	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   180	  ιA' : Type
   181	  ιB' : Type
   182	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   183	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   184	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   185	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   186	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   187	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   188	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   189	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   190	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   191	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   192	
   193	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   194	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   195	
   196	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   197	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   198	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   199	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   200	-/
   201	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   202	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   203	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   204	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   205	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   206	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   207	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   208	
   209	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   210	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   211	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   212	-/
   213	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   214	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   215	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   216	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   217	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   218	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   219	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   220	
   221	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   222	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   223	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   224	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
   225	each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
   226	Blueprint
   227	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
   228	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   229	
   230	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   231	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   232	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   233	-/
   234	theorem pauli_soundness :
   235	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   236	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   237	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   238	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   239	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   240	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   241	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   242	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   243	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   244	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   245	  sorry
   246	
   247	end

     4	/-!
     5	# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states
     6	
     7	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     8	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
     9	operator algebra.  The Fourier/orthogonality identities are retained as named
    10	proof obligations for subsequent stages.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    15	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    27	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    28	
    29	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    30	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    31	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    32	-/
    33	inductive PauliKind where
    34	  | X
    35	  | Z
    36	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    37	
    38	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    40	
    41	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    42	character in their statement types. -/
    43	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    44	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    45	
    46	/--
    47	The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`,
    48	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`; paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    50	-/
    51	noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : Op K :=
    52	  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    53	
    54	/--
    55	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
    56	the second operator of `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 529-571; paper
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`).
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : Op K :=
    60	  fun i j => if i = j then phaseSign (binTrace K (b * j)) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
    63	see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
    64	private noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
    65	  match W with
    66	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
    67	  | .X =>
    68	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))
    69	
    70	/--
    71	The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
    72	index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.
    73	This is the vector form of `def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint
    74	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:550-570`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def pauliVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    78	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=
    79	  ∏ i : ι, singlePauliVec W (e i) (x i)
    80	
    81	/--
    82	The rank-one projector onto `pauliVec W e`.  This is the projective measurement
    83	element `τ^W_e` in `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 562-570; paper
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`).
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    87	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    88	  Matrix.vecMulVec (pauliVec W e) (fun x => star (pauliVec W e x))
    89	
    90	/-- A compact operator-valued form of a generalized Pauli observable from
    91	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    93	-/
    94	noncomputable def tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

   203	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)

   263	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   264	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   265	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   266	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   267	-/
   268	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   269	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   270	  let lineEdges :=
   271	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   272	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   273	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   274	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   275	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   276	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   277	  let basisEdges :=
   278	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   279	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   280	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   281	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   282	  let pairEdges :=
   283	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   284	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   285	  let msEdges' :=
   286	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   287	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   288	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   289	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   290	
   291	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   292	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   293	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   294	-/
   295	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   296	
   297	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   298	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   299	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   302	-/
   303	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   304	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   305	
   306	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   307	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   308	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   309	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   310	-/
   311	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   312	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   313	  simp [pauliEdges]
   314	
   315	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   316	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   317	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   318	-/
   319	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   320	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   321	  by
   322	    classical
   323	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   324	    exact
   325	      Distribution.map
   326	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   327	        (fun s =>
   328	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   329	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))

   331	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   332	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   333	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   334	-/
   335	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   336	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   337	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   338	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   339	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   340	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   341	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   342	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   343	  deriving DecidableEq
   344	
   345	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   346	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   347	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   348	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   349	-/
   350	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   351	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   352	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   353	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   354	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   355	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   356	
   357	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   358	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   359	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   360	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   361	-/
   362	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   363	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   364	  toFun
   365	    | .value a => .inl a
   366	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   367	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   368	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   369	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   370	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   371	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   372	  invFun
   373	    | .inl a => .value a
   374	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   375	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   376	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   377	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   378	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   379	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   380	  left_inv := by
   381	    intro x
   382	    cases x <;> rfl
   383	  right_inv := by
   384	    intro x
   385	    cases x with
   386	    | inl a => rfl
   387	    | inr x =>
   388	        cases x with
   389	        | inl a => rfl
   390	        | inr x =>
   391	            cases x with
   392	            | inl a => rfl
   393	            | inr x =>
   394	                cases x with
   395	                | inl a => rfl
   396	                | inr x =>
   397	                    cases x with
   398	                    | inl a => rfl
   399	                    | inr x =>
   400	                        cases x with
   401	                        | inl a => rfl
   402	                        | inr a => rfl
   403	
   404	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   405	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm
   406	
   407	instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
   408	  ⟨.bit 0⟩
   409	
   410	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   411	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   412	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   413	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   414	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   415	-/
   416	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   417	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   418	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   419	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   420	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   421	
   422	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   423	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   424	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   425	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   426	-/
   427	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   428	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   429	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   430	
   431	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   432	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   433	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   434	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   435	-/
   436	def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   437	  match t, a with
   438	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   439	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   440	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   441	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   442	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   443	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   444	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   445	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   446	  | _, _ => false
   447	
   448	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   449	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   450	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   451	-/
   452	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   453	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   454	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   455	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   456	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   457	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   458	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   459	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   460	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   461	
   462	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   463	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   464	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   465	-/
   466	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   467	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   468	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   469	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   470	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   471	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   472	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   473	
   474	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   475	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   476	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   477	-/
   478	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   479	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   480	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   481	
   482	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   483	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   484	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   485	-/
   486	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   487	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   488	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   489	    (match W with
   490	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   491	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   492	
   493	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   494	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   495	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   496	-/
   497	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   498	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   499	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   500	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   501	      (a * (match W with
   502	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   503	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   504	
   505	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   506	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   507	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   508	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   509	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   510	-/
   511	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   512	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   513	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   514	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   515	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   516	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   517	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   518	
   519	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   520	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   521	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   522	-/
   523	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   524	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   525	  open Classical in
   526	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   527	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   528	      if tA = tB then
   529	        decide (a = b)
   530	      else
   531	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   532	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   533	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   534	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   535	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   536	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   538	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   539	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   540	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   541	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   542	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   543	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   544	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   545	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   546	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   547	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   548	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   550	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   552	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   553	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   554	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   555	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   556	          else true
   557	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   558	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   559	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   560	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   561	          else true
   562	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   564	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   566	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   567	    else false
   568	
   569	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   570	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   571	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   572	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   573	-/
   574	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   575	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   576	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   577	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   578	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   579	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   580	  μ_prob := by sorry
   581	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   582	
   583	end
   584	
   585	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap
   165	
   166	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

     4	/-!
     5	# Quantum states and tensor placement for the low individual degree test
     6	
     7	Core quantum-state definitions together with tensor-placement operators.
     8	-/
     9	
    10	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    11	
    12	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    13	
    14	/-- A PSD density matrix indexed by `ι`.
    15	
    16	There is intentionally no global `Inhabited` instance: the zero matrix is PSD but
    17	not a physical state of unit trace, so an ambient default would silently
    18	trivialize later statements. Use `IsNormalized` to additionally require
    19	`τ(ρ) = 1`.
    20	
    21	This remains the ambient state space for the current LDT development: strategy
    22	packages in `LDT/Test/StrategyCore.lean`, the SWAP-symmetry API `PermInvState`,
    23	and the expectation-value lemmas in `LDT/Basic/OperatorExpectations.lean` are all
    24	stated for arbitrary density matrices, not only pure states. -/
    25	structure QuantumState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] where
    26	  density : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 0
    27	  density_psd : 0 ≤ density := by positivity
    28	
    29	/-- Unit normalized trace for the concrete matrix carried by a state. -/
    30	def QuantumState.IsNormalized {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) : Prop :=
    32	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 1
    33	
    34	/-- A normalized state has a nonempty carrier: if the carrier were empty, the
    35	trace would vanish and `normalizedTrace = 0 / 0 = 0`, contradicting `= 1`. -/
    36	theorem QuantumState.IsNormalized.nonempty {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    37	    {ψ : QuantumState ι} (hψ : ψ.IsNormalized) : Nonempty ι := by
    38	  by_contra h
    39	  rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
    40	  letI := h
    41	  rw [QuantumState.IsNormalized] at hψ
    42	  have hzero : MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 0 := by
    43	    simp [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace]
    44	  exact zero_ne_one (hzero.symm.trans hψ)
    45	
    46	/-- The scaled rank-one density matrix attached to a state vector.
    47	
    48	Because this development uses the normalized trace `τ(A) = tr(A) / dim`, the
    49	quantum state represented by a unit vector `ψ` is `dim · |ψ⟩⟨ψ|` rather than the
    50	raw projector `|ψ⟩⟨ψ|`. This scaling makes `τ(ρ) = 1` and keeps `ev` aligned
    51	with the paper's bra-ket expectations. -/
    52	noncomputable def pureDensity {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    53	    (ψ : ι → ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι :=
    54	  (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) • Matrix.vecMulVec ψ (star ψ)
    55	
    56	/-- Swap the two tensor coordinates of a bipartite state vector. -/
    57	def swapVector {ι : Type*} (ψ : ι × ι → ℂ) : ι × ι → ℂ :=
    58	  fun ij => ψ (ij.2, ij.1)
    59	
    60	/-- A pure-state witness as a unit vector in the ambient finite Hilbert space.
    61	
    62	The associated density matrix is `pureDensity ψ.vector = dim · |ψ⟩⟨ψ|`, so that
    63	coercing to `QuantumState` preserves the paper's scalar `⟨ψ|X|ψ⟩` formulas
    64	despite our use of the normalized trace. -/
    65	structure PureState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] where
    66	  vector : ι → ℂ
    67	  unit : star vector ⬝ᵥ vector = 1

    69	namespace PureState

   124	theorem normalizedTrace_density_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   125	    (ψ : PureState ι) (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
   126	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ((ψ : QuantumState ι).density * X) =
   127	      star ψ.vector ⬝ᵥ (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) := by
   128	  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   129	  calc
   130	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ((ψ : QuantumState ι).density * X)
   131	      = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (X * (ψ : QuantumState ι).density) := by
   132	          rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_mul_comm]
   133	    _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (X * ψ.density) := by rfl
   134	    _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   135	          ((Fintype.card ι : ℂ) • (X * Matrix.vecMulVec ψ.vector (star ψ.vector))) := by
   136	          simp [density, pureDensity]
   137	    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
   138	          MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (X * Matrix.vecMulVec ψ.vector (star ψ.vector)) := by
   139	          rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_smul]
   140	    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
   141	          (((X * Matrix.vecMulVec ψ.vector (star ψ.vector)).trace) /
   142	            (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)) := by
   143	          simp [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace]
   144	    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
   145	          (((Matrix.vecMulVec (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) (star ψ.vector)).trace) /
   146	            (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)) := by
   147	          rw [Matrix.mul_vecMulVec]
   148	    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
   149	          (((X *ᵥ ψ.vector) ⬝ᵥ star ψ.vector) / (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)) := by
   150	          rw [Matrix.trace_vecMulVec]
   151	    _ = (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) ⬝ᵥ star ψ.vector := by
   152	          field_simp [hcard]
   153	    _ = star ψ.vector ⬝ᵥ (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) := by
   154	          rw [dotProduct_comm]

   414	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁)
   415	    (C : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   416	    rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) A * opTensor B C = opTensor B (A * C) := by
   417	  calc
   418	    rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) A * opTensor B C
   419	        = rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) A *
   420	            (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) B * rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) C) := by
   421	          rw [leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor]
   422	    _ = (rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) A * leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) B) *
   423	          rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) C := by
   424	          rw [Matrix.mul_assoc]
   425	    _ = opTensor B A * rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) C := by
   426	          rw [rightTensor_mul_leftTensor_eq_opTensor]
   427	    _ = (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) B * rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) A) *
   428	          rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) C := by
   429	          rw [leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor]
   430	    _ = leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) B *
   431	          (rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) A * rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) C) := by
   432	          rw [Matrix.mul_assoc]
   433	    _ = leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) B * rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (A * C) := by
   434	          rw [rightTensor_mul_rightTensor]
   435	    _ = opTensor B (A * C) := by
   436	          rw [leftTensor_mul_rightTensor_eq_opTensor]
   437	
   438	/-- Conjugate transpose distributes over `opTensor`. -/
   439	theorem conjTranspose_opTensor
   440	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   441	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   442	    (opTensor A B)ᴴ = opTensor Aᴴ Bᴴ :=
   443	  Matrix.conjTranspose_kronecker A B
   444	
   445	/-- Conjugate transpose commutes with left tensor placement. -/
   446	@[simp]
   447	theorem leftTensor_conjTranspose
   448	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   449	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) :
   450	    (leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) A)ᴴ = leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) Aᴴ := by
   451	  simpa [leftTensor, opTensor] using
   452	    (conjTranspose_opTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (ι₂ := ι₂) A (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂))
   453	
   454	/-- Conjugate transpose commutes with right tensor placement. -/
   455	@[simp]
   456	theorem rightTensor_conjTranspose
   457	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   458	    (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   459	    (rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) B)ᴴ = rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) Bᴴ := by
   460	  simpa [rightTensor, opTensor] using
   461	    (conjTranspose_opTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (ι₂ := ι₂) (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) B)
   462	
   463	/-- `opTensor` distributes over multiplication. -/
   464	theorem opTensor_mul
   465	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   466	    (A₁ A₂ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B₁ B₂ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   467	    opTensor A₁ B₁ * opTensor A₂ B₂ = opTensor (A₁ * A₂) (B₁ * B₂) :=
   468	  (Matrix.mul_kronecker_mul A₁ A₂ B₁ B₂).symm
   469	
   470	/-- `opTensor` is linear in the left factor: subtraction. -/
   471	theorem opTensor_sub_left
   472	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   473	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (C : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   474	    opTensor A C - opTensor B C = opTensor (A - B) C := by
   475	  simpa [opTensor] using
   476	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_sub_left (A₁ := A) (A₂ := B) (B := C)
   477	
   478	/-- Left tensor placement commutes with subtraction. -/
   479	theorem leftTensor_sub
   480	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   481	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) :
   482	    leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) A - leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) B =
   483	      leftTensor (ι₂ := ι₂) (A - B) := by
   484	  simpa [leftTensor, opTensor, Matrix.kronecker] using
   485	    (opTensor_sub_left (ι₁ := ι₁) (ι₂ := ι₂) A B (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂))
   486	
   487	/-- Right tensor placement commutes with subtraction. -/
   488	theorem rightTensor_sub
   489	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   490	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   491	    rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) A - rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) B =
   492	      rightTensor (ι₁ := ι₁) (A - B) := by
   493	  simpa [rightTensor, opTensor] using
   494	    (MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_sub_right
   495	      (A := (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁)) (B₁ := A) (B₂ := B))
   496	
   497	/-- `opTensor` is linear in the left factor: real scalar multiplication. -/
   498	theorem opTensor_smul_left_error
   499	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   500	    (c : Error) (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   501	    opTensor (c • A) B = c • opTensor A B := by
   502	  ext x y
   503	  simp [opTensor, mul_comm, mul_left_comm]
   504	
   505	/-- `opTensor` is linear in the right factor: real scalar multiplication. -/
   506	theorem opTensor_smul_right_error
   507	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   508	    (c : Error) (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   509	    opTensor A (c • B) = c • opTensor A B := by
   510	  ext x y
   511	  simp [opTensor, mul_comm, mul_left_comm]
   512	
   513	/-- `opTensor` is additive in the left factor. -/
   514	theorem opTensor_add_left_local
   515	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   516	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (C : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   517	    opTensor (A + B) C = opTensor A C + opTensor B C := by
   518	  ext x y
   519	  simp [opTensor, add_mul]
   520	
   521	/-- `opTensor` is additive in the right factor. -/
   522	theorem opTensor_add_right_local
   523	    {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   524	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B C : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   525	    opTensor A (B + C) = opTensor A B + opTensor A C := by
   526	  ext x y
   527	  simp [opTensor, mul_add]
   528	
   529	/-- Pull a finite sum out of the left factor of `opTensor`. -/
   530	theorem opTensor_sum_left_finset
   531	    {α ι₁ ι₂ : Type*}
   532	    [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   533	    (s : Finset α) (f : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   534	    opTensor (∑ a ∈ s, f a) B = ∑ a ∈ s, opTensor (f a) B := by
   535	  classical
   536	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   537	  | empty => simp [opTensor]
   538	  | @insert a s ha ih =>
   539	      rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha, opTensor_add_left_local, ih]
   540
